title: Can a Handyman Replace Light Fixtures and Fix Leaky Faucets in Ontario?
seoTitle: Handyman vs Plumber vs Electrician in Ontario | Collingwood
seoDescription: Can a handyman replace a light fixture or fix a leaky faucet in Ontario? Learn how to route general repairs, plumbing fixtures, ceiling fans and electrical…
html:
Short answer: a handyman may be suitable for some visible, contained home repairs and accessible plumbing-fixture work. Electrical work performed for hire is different: in Ontario, it generally must be completed by a Licensed Electrical Contractor or by an electrician working for one. If your list includes both a dripping faucet and a light-fixture replacement, separate the work by trade before booking.

That distinction does not mean every faucet problem needs a plumber or every repair needs a specialist. It means the decision should be based on the system involved, the location of the problem and whether the work could involve concealed damage, new wiring or changes to building systems.

When a handyman may be a reasonable fit

A general handyman may be appropriate for a visible repair that is limited in scope and does not involve electrical wiring, concealed plumbing or a larger structural problem. Examples may include:

  • Adjusting doors, hinges, handles, locks and cabinet hardware
  • Repairing trim, drawers, shelving and weather stripping
  • Completing minor drywall, caulking, painting or finishing work after the underlying issue is resolved
  • Replacing an accessible plumbing fixture when the shut-off works and there is no sign of a hidden leak
  • Replacing a faucet component or toilet component when the cause is identifiable and contained

Collingwood Handyman's home repair service page describes everyday repair work including leaky faucets, doors, drawers, railings, weatherization and fixture-related work. Confirm the exact scope before work starts, especially if the repair could involve a wall, floor, ceiling or supply and drain piping.

Why a light-fixture replacement needs a separate check

A light fixture is connected to the home's electrical installation. ESA states that, with limited exemptions, only a Licensed Electrical Contractor is legally authorized to perform electrical work in a home for hire. A general contractor or handyperson cannot take on the electrical portion unless the work is performed through an appropriately licensed electrical contracting business.

ESA also says that the requirement applies no matter how small the electrical job appears. Before approving a fixture replacement, ask for the electrical contracting business's ECRA/ESA licence number and confirm who will perform the work. The contractor should handle the required electrical notification of work rather than asking you to file it on the contractor's behalf.

For more detail, review ESA's guidance on who can do electrical work at your property and how to hire a Licensed Electrical Contractor.

Ceiling fans combine electrical and mounting work

Ceiling fans can involve both physical mounting and electrical connections. The existing electrical box may not be suitable for the fan, and the scope may include support, wiring, a switch or control and testing. Ask in advance which business is responsible for the electrical portion.

Collingwood Handyman has a ceiling fan installation service page. Even when a service page discusses installation, Ontario homeowners should confirm whether the electrical work will be completed by a Licensed Electrical Contractor and whether the required ESA notification will be filed.

When a faucet or toilet problem should go to a plumber

A contained fixture issue may be suitable for the provider's stated scope. Contact a plumber promptly when the problem involves diagnosis or repair beyond the fixture itself, such as:

  • A leak inside a wall, ceiling or floor
  • Water damage that is spreading, still wet or affecting structural materials
  • Changes to supply, drain or vent piping
  • A frozen or burst pipe
  • A corroded, seized or damaged shut-off valve
  • Low water pressure affecting several fixtures
  • Sewer odours, wastewater backup or contaminated water

If water is actively escaping, shut off the supply if it is safe to do so, protect nearby finishes and arrange diagnosis before cosmetic repairs. Drywall, painting or trim work can follow the source repair; it should not replace it.

Use a trade-routing checklist for a mixed repair list

Work itemPossible first callWhat to confirm
Doors, trim, shelving, cabinets, drywall or caulkingHandyman, if visible and containedWhether the issue is non-structural and within the provider's scope
Faucet, aerator or toilet componentHandyman or plumber, depending on the causeWhether the shut-off works and whether there is hidden damage or piping work
Light fixture, ceiling fan, switch, outlet or new wiringLicensed Electrical ContractorThe ECRA/ESA licence number, electrical scope and notification of work

For a quote request, list each repair separately. Include photographs, the fixture model if known, the location of shut-offs and a short description of what happens when the problem occurs. If a property is seasonal or vacant, mention that as well. Clear information helps the provider identify work that may need another trade before the visit.

Electrical notifications and building permits are different

ESA explains that almost all electrical work requires a notification of work, often called an electrical permit, and that the person doing the work or the Licensed Electrical Contractor must file it. A municipal building permit is a separate process. Ontario advises homeowners to contact their local building department when they are unsure whether renovation or repair work requires a building permit.

Review the ESA notification and inspection guidance and the Ontario building-permit guide before work that changes walls, structure, use or building systems.

Questions to ask before booking

  • Which items on the list are within your scope?
  • Does any item involve electrical wiring, a switch, outlet, new box or concealed connection?
  • If electrical work is required, what is the ECRA/ESA licence number of the contracting business?
  • Will the electrical contractor file the ESA notification of work?
  • Could the plumbing issue involve a hidden leak, piping or water damage?
  • Which materials, access requirements and exclusions should appear in the estimate?
  • Are any permits or municipal approvals worth confirming before work begins?

Requesting help from Collingwood Handyman

For a contained repair list in Collingwood or a nearby service area, describe each item separately rather than writing only "general repairs." Include photos, measurements where useful, fixture information and access limitations. The Collingwood Handyman contact page provides the quote route and lists 705-795-4009 for project enquiries.

The practical rule is simple: use a handyman for suitable general repairs and contained fixture work, involve a plumber when the water-system problem is hidden, active or beyond the fixture, and use a Licensed Electrical Contractor for electrical work performed for hire in Ontario.
